scope: Installed Apollo display controls; compositor and keyboard validation on an isolated nested display, with the actual device accelerometer

checks: default service does not claim the accelerometer or create preferences
portrait matches compositor and touch transforms
landscape-left matches compositor and touch transforms
portrait-inverted matches compositor and touch transforms
landscape-right matches compositor and touch transforms
lock preserves the current landscape orientation
invalid orientation is rejected without changing preferences or monitor
invalid refresh selection is rejected without changing preferences
an unadvertised refresh mode is rejected with the display unchanged
a real preference-write failure restores the previous monitor and touch state
automatic rotation claims the actual device accelerometer
actual sensor orientation is represented by a matching transform
manual orientation releases the actual accelerometer claim
saved orientation is restored after a real compositor configuration reload
the test compositor returns to its base transform while the service is stopped
service restart restores the persisted orientation
the real keyboard reserves 180 logical pixels in landscape
the real keyboard reserves 300 logical pixels in portrait
the actual GTK settings window renders inside the private compositor
the settings window closes normally through a window-manager request
the tested compositor has no configuration errors
preferences are private and contain only display settings
the display controller exits normally and releases its sensor connection

limits: The virtual compositor checks monitor and touch configuration, not physical finger coordinates.
The actual accelerometer was claimed, read and released; the phone was not physically turned through every orientation.
The physical panel advertises 60, 90, 120 and 144 Hz; switching its refresh rate was not acceptance-tested in this phase.
No measured battery benefit, physical automatic-rotation acceptance or cold-boot result is claimed.
The physical PIN setup and owner credentials were not used by the isolated test.
